metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: On question answering HotpotQA and fact verification Fever, ReAct overcomes prevalent hallucination and error propagation in chain-of-thought reasoning by interacting with a simple Wikipedia API and generates human-like task-solving trajectories that are more interpretable than baselines without reasoning traces. On interactive decision making benchmarks ALFWorld and WebShop, ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by an absolute success rate of 34% and 10% respectively, while being prompt-based and improving human interpretability and trustworthiness.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Toolformer achieves substantially improved zero-shot performance across a variety of downstream tasks, often competitive with much larger models, without sacrificing its core language modeling abilities. Toolformer still lags behind the much larger GPT-3 175B model.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Reflexion obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks including sequential decision-making, coding, and language reasoning. On the HumanEval coding benchmark, Reflexion achieves 91% pass@1 accuracy, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: ToT significantly enhances problem solving on three novel tasks requiring non-trivial planning or search. On Game of 24, GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting solves 4% of tasks while ToT achieves 74% success rate. Oracle best DFS state selection further improves performance, solving 7/20 games in the evaluated set. Improvements are also reported for Creative Writing and Mini Crosswords.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models.

evaluated_datasets: APIBench, a comprehensive dataset consisting of HuggingFace, TorchHub, and TensorHub APIs.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Gorilla surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls. When combined with a document retriever, Gorilla demonstrates strong capability to adapt to test-time document changes, enabling flexible user updates or version changes, and substantially mitigates hallucination commonly encountered when prompting LLMs directly.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs.

evaluated_datasets: Evaluated in MineDojo, an open-source Minecraft AI framework. Baselines include ReAct, Reflexion, and AutoGPT re-interpreted for MineDojo. Evaluation metrics cover exploration performance, tech tree mastery, map coverage, and zero-shot generalization to novel tasks in a new world.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: VOYAGER demonstrates strong in-context lifelong learning. It obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer distances, and unlocks key tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA. It builds an ever-growing reusable, interpretable, generalizable skill library and can utilize it in a new Minecraft world to solve novel tasks from scratch, while other methods struggle to generalize.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models.

metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: On code generation benchmarks, MetaGPT achieves state-of-the-art Pass@1 of 85.9% on HumanEval and 87.7% on MBPP. On collaborative software engineering benchmarks it generates more coherent solutions than previous chat-based multi-agent systems, outperforming frameworks such as AutoGPT for complex software project creation.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework.

evaluated_datasets: AGENTBENCH comprises 8 distinct environments for real-world challenges. Datasets, environments and an integrated evaluation package are released at https://github.com/THUDM/AgentBench. Evaluation is conducted on 29 LLMs, API-based and OSS, across the 8 environments.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Extensive tests over 29 API-based and open-sourced LLMs show top commercial LLMs present strong ability of acting as agents in complex environments, with a significant disparity in performance between them and many OSS competitors no larger than 70B. Typical failure reasons are poor long-term reasoning, decision-making and instruction following abilities, which are main obstacles for usable LLM agents. Improving instruction following and training on high quality multi-round alignment data could improve agent performance. Training on code presents ambivalent impacts on different agent tasks. Overall scores across the 8 environments are reported with average lines for two LLM types.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents.

evaluated_datasets: No specific benchmark datasets are named in the provided context; empirical studies are described across example applications in mathematics, coding, question answering, operations research, online decision-making, entertainment, etc.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Empirical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in many example applications spanning mathematics, coding, question answering, operations research, online decision-making, entertainment, etc. Customizable and conversable agents enable rapid creation of role-specific agents e.g., code writer, code executor, human feedback wiring, output validation with autonomous multi-turn conversation and optional human solicitation. Conversation programming streamlines development of intricate LLM application workflows via defining agents and flexible conversation patterns.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation.

evaluated_datasets: SWE-bench consisting of 2,294 software engineering problems from real GitHub issues and pull requests across 12 popular Python repositories. Evaluation uses the issue description plus codebase context and verifies generated edits by running unit tests. Retrieval analysis compares BM25 retrieval to oracle retrieval for providing relevant files within token limits.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Both state-of-the-art proprietary models and the fine-tuned SWE-Llama can resolve only the simplest issues. Best-performing model Claude 2 solves a mere 1.96% of the issues. BM25 retrieval vs oracle: approximately 40% of instances BM25 retrieves a superset of the oracle files for the 27,000-token context limit, but in almost half of the instances with the 27,000-token limit it retrieves none of the files from the oracle context.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?.

evaluated_datasets: Open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and long-form generation tasks.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: SELF-RAG 7B and 13B significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on a diverse set of tasks. Specifically, SELF-RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generation.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection.

Primary architectural approach represented is 'Multi-Agent Collaboration' focused on iterative and structured reasoning.
Most widespread cross-cutting limitation is 'Inference Latency & Token / Computational Overhead', impacting 10 of 12 paper(s).
